# Coordinate Agents

> Local Web Workspace for coding-agent terminal pairs. Default Collaboration
> uses Codex to clarify, delegate and review, and Antigravity to implement.
> Custom Terminals supports two user-selected CLI executables and optional prompts.

## Product and version boundary

The main entry is Web Workspace, not a Skill installer or Task Graph orchestrator.
Node.js >=18 and Git are required. Agent CLIs and provider login are installed
and managed separately. No Codex Plugin or global npm install is required for Web.

As checked on 2026-10-20, npm dist-tags.latest is 3.0.1. Current source includes
later Git Changes/review feedback, Custom Terminals, desktop notifications,
Collaboration Timeline, and Collaboration Health. Use source for those additions;
a merge to main does not publish npm. Package and Plugin versions are independent.

Published: npx @hogancv/coordinate-agents@latest web --root "/path/to/project" --port 3000
Current source: npm ci, then node bin/coordinate-agents.mjs web --root "/path/to/project" --port 3000
Use --port 0 for a free port. The startup directory is registered automatically;
a non-Git startup folder initializes Git/storage without a commit.

npm 3.x exposes web, help, version and Web --root/--port/--json only. It excludes
Skill installation, Legacy CLI, structured Task/Graph API, MCP server, read-only
Inspector, and public Adapter SDK. Do not use npm latest for install/doctor/config/
quickstart/task/inspector. Those require the Plugin, source Legacy entry, or npm 2.4.0.

## Web behavior and limits

Each task creates fresh task-bound Sessions; Custom also binds each terminal slot.
Default commands are codex and agy, with executable overrides in project settings.
Workspace settings allow choosing Antigravity tool permission mode (prompt by default,
or --dangerously-skip-permissions for automatic tool approval). Project/user args override it;
args: [] opts out. Custom Terminals retain their separate Generic CLI configuration.
Custom supports the same CLI twice. Commands are executable names or absolute
paths, without inline arguments or shell syntax. Custom prompt defaults are saved
per project; each task snapshots commands/prompts, including for restart.
Shared prompts are bounded to 8 KB UTF-8, each terminal prompt to 4 KB.
Custom prompt delivery requires explicit readiness/multiline-paste confirmation;
unknown CLI readiness is not inferred. Custom has no default roles, rounds, or
Send to Codex review feedback. Diff viewing/copying remains available.

Default prompt version is 2.3.0-web-lite-3. The task-supplied workspace-message.mjs
helper supports send/read/wait/report/changes with saved task/session binding.
Web does not automatically invoke Skills, scan Agent Bus, restore structured
Tasks, discover plugins, or create Task/Graph records. Pending wait is not
permission to resend. Terminal output and idle do not prove completion.
SENT confirms dispatch only; WORKING, DONE, REVIEWING, CHANGES_REQUESTED,
APPROVED and FAILED are formal agent reports, not independently verified facts.
Workspace task status is terminal lifecycle, not implementation or review completion.
Role prompts are not an enforced state machine, sandbox, or technical release gate.
They require user authorization for commit/push/release. Web tasks share one
project worktree; creating a terminal pair does not create an isolated worktree.

Git Changes shows current working-tree diffs, including earlier user edits,
not an agent-only diff or committed history. Default feedback requires a blank
Codex input prompt and fresh confirmation per send. Preflight cancellation on
file change, diff refresh or drawer close prevents pending dispatch.
Timeline persists recorded round history across refresh/server/pair restart.
History not recorded by earlier versions cannot be reconstructed.
Health shows missing receipts and Session facts; silence is not proof of failure.
It never dispatches, retries, restarts or sends desktop notifications.
Desktop notifications are opt-in per project, Windows 10/11 and macOS only;
Linux is unsupported. Only formal Default receipts trigger them. Dispatch is
at most once per project/task/round/status and OS acceptance is not visible proof.
The browser can close while backend/agents/interactive OS session continue running.

Refresh reconnects to independent Session Hosts. Browser/server shutdown does
not itself close agents; use explicit close/restart controls. Archive closes
associated terminals and hides records, preserving project source. Clearing
archived conversations permanently removes stored task/timeline history.
Recovery actions in source f9f0210 and later (package remains 3.0.1): Reopen task
uses the saved original Codex UUID; without one, the fallback accepts an exact
local primary CLI UUID. Recover executor preserves live owned Codex and opens
only a missing Antigravity session. Both current owned terminals must finish
startup with no identity conflict; no /status or extra UUID confirmation is
required. Legacy AWAITING_CONFIRMATION is read compatibility, not a required step.
Bound/reserved Default tasks refuse fresh-pair restart; use New task for a new
context. Recovery never replays old work, and a new executor cannot complete an
old executor's round. Close confirmations and send-readiness confirmations remain.
Current action table: https://hogancv.github.io/coordinate-agents/codex-conversation-resume.html#action-table
Earlier Resume v1 designs and macOS acceptance reports describe their historical
manual-confirmation stage, not the current flow; see their applicability banners.
Data under .agent-bus and the user project registry is local plaintext.
Agent providers still receive data according to each CLI's configuration.
Server is loopback-only; per-launch capability and Host/Origin checks are not
multi-user authentication. HTTP root binding does not sandbox agent commands.

## v2.4 historical documentation and migration

v2.4 already had lightweight Web collaboration. v3 changes the main product and
npm distribution to Web-first; it does not delete the structured source.
Original v2.4.0 docs and v3 migration: https://hogancv.github.io/coordinate-agents/v2.4.html
Original release docs are pinned to commit 3e36942ce52004ad3136c6f24be57a8255361c75.
Current pages marked v2.4 lineage follow retained Plugin/Legacy code and can
include later corrections; do not treat them as immutable v2.4.0 snapshots.
Web tasks do not automatically convert or replace structured Task/Graph records.

## Optional structured workflow

The repository retains a local-first coordination protocol and runtime through
the GitHub Plugin / Legacy CLI / MCP. Agent Bus, durable Tasks, implementation
evidence, recorded review, Task Graphs, Intent Maps, and explicit recovery are
separate from Web task receipts. Codex and Antigravity are reference adapters;
generic-cli and trusted-local Contract v1 adapters extend the default reference workflow.
Planner/Implementer/Reviewer roles are configurable in that structured runtime.

Install Plugin with codex plugin marketplace add hogancv/coordinate-agents, then
codex plugin add coordinate-agents@coordinate-agents. It bundles its runtime
and does not require a global npm CLI. Source Legacy entry is
node bin/coordinate-agents-legacy.mjs; published Legacy CLI must pin 2.4.0.
Structured Tasks record a non-owning sessionId and can reuse a healthy Session
through review rework. Failed/exited Sessions require explicit recovery/dispatch.
Task Graph contracts provide explicit isolated-worktree dispatch, bounded waves,
facts-first recovery, aggregate integration and review. REVIEW_APPROVED is not
RELEASE_APPROVED. Never infer release authorization from an implementation receipt.
The read-only Inspector is a separate Legacy UI, absent from npm 3.x Web.
